comment: Inventory of source-backed native-lowering candidates for the Crash of the Titans (Wii) native port. A candidate is a guest function that was sampled in the CPU capture AND whose C/C++ source was recovered in this repository (src/c, src/master_match, src/external, src/radical). Addresses are deduplicated: all host symbols that map to the same guest address (func_X, func_X.cold, func_X_kernel, native_guest_primary_X / native_guest_resume_X / native_guest_continuation_X) are aggregated into one row and their samples summed. The sample share is reported both against ALL guest timer samples in the capture window (the capture summary's denominator, 42211) and against the NON-EXTERNAL guest samples (42211 minus the 2015 samples attributed to the '<external>' module, i.e. 40196); the non-external denominator is the one to use when comparing against 'generated guest code' shares, because '<external>' is not guest code at all. Decision policy: (1) excluded -> rejected (effect-exclusions.json); (2) already replaced by an existing NATIVE body (adopted plain-leaf kernel, linked-region promotion) -> rejected as already covered; (3) captured cost below 10 samples -> rejected as below the qualification threshold; (4) everything else is a candidate. 'exact_evidence_kind' is deliberately strict: 're-verified exact now' means the repository's own verification path was executed in this session and returned exact (byte+size+relocation identical to orig/main.dol); 'manifest-recorded exact' means the hash-pinned admission manifest records it but the admission path itself could not be re-run in this session. No cached, report-only or search-discovered hit is described as exact.

capture.denominator_note: share_of_guest_samples uses all 42211 guest timer samples in the capture window (matches the capture summary's categories). share_of_non_external_guest_samples uses 40196 samples, i.e. the same window minus the 2015 '<external>' module samples, because '<external>' is not guest code and the candidate pool is entirely guest code.

frozen_overlap.note: the held-out spec was used only to exclude addresses; it was not inspected per target and was not used as retrieval or training data. The 500 addresses in native-port/reference/guest-regions/effect-exclusions.json are the SAME 500 addresses, so the exclusion policy and the frozen benchmark are one partition (see 'exclusion_pool').

exclusion_pool.note: these guest addresses are excluded from optimisation material and are therefore not used as lowering candidates. Independently verified in this session: the exclusion list is EXACTLY the held-out frozen 500-function benchmark set (scripts/match/master_match.py::frozen_addresses() returns the same 500 addresses, set equality confirmed), so the effect-exclusion policy and the frozen-isolation policy are the same partition. The candidate pool is disjoint from it, hence frozen-clean by construction; this is not independent evidence of non-frozenness.

func_802DADD0.note: the capture summary calls this function out as prominent but excluded; it has no recovered source, so it is not a candidate and must not be used as optimisation material

totals.headroom_note: the source-backed pool is capped at the candidate share: every other sampled guest function (including the largest ones, e.g. func_803143EC 2792 samples, func_803DB050 496, func_802FDB74 371, func_802DD268 365, func_801B721C 273) has no recovered source and is therefore out of scope for a source-backed lowering

candidates.reason: rejected: the source-backed kernel is 10-13% SLOWER than the plain-leaf kernel already installed (77 vs 68 ns/call unwatched) because it goes through the MMU check per access while the plain-leaf kernel reads raw MEM1; it is only faster (0.75x) when a watch sits on the data page. There is also no observable-register gain: the plain-leaf kernel already leaves the same f0..f7/ps1 values.
